Trumped-up means deliberately invented or fabricated — especially to harm someone or to justify something unfair.

When something is trumped-up, it is not just false. It is purposely made up by someone with a bad or dishonest intention. The lie is created as a tool — to punish, blame, manipulate, or deceive.

Think of it this way: if someone does not have a real reason to accuse you of something, but they invent a reason anyway — just to get you in trouble or to justify doing something unfair to you — that invented reason is trumped-up.

The word almost always carries two ideas at once:

  • Something is false (not real, not true).
  • That falsehood was deliberately created by someone with a dishonest motive.

If you remove either of these two ideas, you lose the full meaning of the word. A simple mistake is not trumped-up. An accidental misunderstanding is not trumped-up. The word always implies conscious, calculated deception.
What It Is Almost Always Used With

"Trumped-up" is almost exclusively paired with words related to accusations, legal charges, or stated reasons. The most common combinations are:

  • Trumped-up charges — false criminal accusations invented against someone
  • Trumped-up allegations — fake claims made against someone to damage them
  • Trumped-up accusations — invented blame with no real basis
  • Trumped-up reasons / excuses — false justifications given for an action

You will almost never see "trumped-up" used to describe a physical object or a neutral situation. It lives in the world of blame, accusations, and justifications.

The journalist was arrested on trumped-up charges of espionage — everyone knew it was the government's way of silencing her.

Here, the charges of espionage were invented. She was not a spy. The accusation was fabricated specifically to have a reason to arrest her.

He was fired on trumped-up grounds — his boss claimed he violated company policy, but the "violation" was something the boss invented after the fact.

The boss created a fake rule-breaking story to justify firing him. The reason was not real.

The rival company sued them on trumped-up claims, hoping to drain their money and slow them down.

The legal claims had no real foundation. They were made up as a business weapon.
The Moral Weight of the Word

"Trumped-up" is a word with strong negative moral weight. When you use it, you are saying:

  • Someone is being treated unjustly.
  • The accusation or reason being used against them is a lie.
  • That lie was deliberately constructed by someone with power or an agenda.

It often appears in contexts involving power imbalances — a government targeting a citizen, a powerful person going after a weaker one, or an institution using false justifications to act against someone who cannot easily fight back. Because of this, the word carries a sense of injustice and manipulation.
How It Differs From Similar Words

IdeaWhat it lacks compared to "trumped-up"
FalseJust means untrue — no implication of intent or harm
FakeGeneral — doesn't specifically suggest it was made to harm someone
FabricatedClose, but more neutral — can be used in non-harmful contexts
Made-upInformal and general — could describe a harmless story

False simply means something is not true, but it carries no suggestion of harmful intent. Fake is general and can describe anything imitated or artificial. Fabricated comes closest, but it is more neutral — you can fabricate a story for fun or for art. Made-up is casual and can describe anything imaginary, even an innocent bedtime story.

Trumped-up, by contrast, is always about deliberate, harmful deception — specifically designed to unjustly blame, accuse, or justify something against a person.

Trumped-up describes an accusation, charge, or reason that someone has deliberately invented — not because it is true, but because they need a false justification to harm, blame, or take unfair action against someone.
A Real-World Way to Remember It

Imagine a powerful person wants to throw someone in jail, but that person has done nothing wrong. So the powerful person makes up a crime, hires false witnesses, and creates fake evidence. That manufactured, invented, dishonest accusation? That is a trumped-up charge. The victim is innocent. The accusation is a weapon, not a truth.

That is the word in its full, sharp meaning.
